`assets/skills/habeas-refactor/SKILL.md` has front matter and is a bundled skill, so `requirements.cli.skill_conventions` applies. It meets each obligation.

- **Description states when to use it, in terms of the user's task.** It begins "Use when a change moves code, tests, or requirements ... to another file, chapter, or outline node". It gives concrete cases: moving a function, renaming or splitting a file, splitting or merging modules or chapters, and moving a requirement to another chapter.
- **Description names the neighboring bundled skills.** It names `habeas-requirements` for changing what code or requirements say. It names `habeas-evidence` for reassessing stale evidence. It names `habeas-bootstrap-requirements` for deriving an initial requirement set. These are the three other skills under `assets/skills`.

The `## Rules` section comes after it. The sibling `habeas-evidence` skill has the same layout. I read the short orientation as part of the opening and not as displacing the workflow.
- **Specialized material in referenced files.** The requirement only permits this (MAY). This skill has no extra files and puts everything inline, so nothing is required here.

The site query returned no violation matches to judge. I found no gap.
